summary:
Lunar Navigator is an interactive 3D lunar exploration and landing-site analysis application designed to help identify promising landing locations and mission windows near the Moon’s south pole.
Developed using Unity, C#, Python, and Fast API, the application combines an immersive lunar environment with scientific calculations based on real NASA JPL Horizons data. Users can select a lunar site, choose a landing date and mission duration, and evaluate sunlight availability, direct-to-Earth visibility, and potential communication blackout periods. The Opportunity Finder also compares candidate sites and landing times against user-defined mission requirements to recommend suitable options.
Lunar Navigator addresses the challenge by transforming complex astronomical data into accessible visualizations, interactive timelines, and practical mission-planning insights. Its current scientific model evaluates geometric visibility rather than terrain obstruction.
This project is important because sunlight and Earth visibility are critical considerations for lunar surface operations. By making these conditions easier to understand and compare, Lunar Navigator supports informed exploration, education, and early-stage mission planning.
details:
Lunar Navigator is an interactive 3D lunar landing-site analysis application developed with Unity, C#, Python, and Fast API.

Users can explore the Moon, select south-pole reference locations, choose a landing date and mission duration, and analyze sunlight availability, Earth visibility, and potential communication interruptions using real NASA JPL Horizons data. An Opportunity Finder searches different locations and landing times against user-defined mission requirements.

The project transforms complex astronomical calculations into accessible 3D visualizations, timelines, and mission-planning metrics. We considered scientific accuracy, usability, configurable mission requirements, data provenance, and computational limits.

Its current scientific model calculates geometric visibility, without verified terrain obstruction. Lunar Navigator is intended to support education, exploration, and preliminary mission comparisons—not certify landing safety.
dataRefs: NASA/JPL Horizons: Official documentation for the NASA Horizons API, which we use to retrieve real Sun and Earth positions for lunar visibility calculations and landing opportunity predictions.
NASA Moon to Mars Lunar Surface Data Book: Official NASA report used to obtain reference coordinates for Shackleton Rim, Connecting Ridge, and Malapert Massif (Table A2.1-1, page 75).
